- When sentiment is consistently low (≤0.27) over recent days, model tends to overcorrect downward; adjust forecast downward by 1–2% to avoid undershoot.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >5% from prior peak), model often overshoots and fails to mean-revert; reduce forecast by 3–5% in next 3–5 days.
- If sentiment is high (≥0.77) and price is trending up, model frequently overestimates; cap forecast at 1–2% above recent high or use sentiment-weighted moving average.
- When sentiment swings sharply (e.g., from 0.80 to 0.00), model often misreads momentum; delay forecast adjustment until sentiment stabilizes or use 3-day lagged sentiment filter.
- For 30-day horizon, model tends to overestimate mean reversion; apply a 1–3% downward bias if sentiment is neutral or slightly negative.
- If sentiment is consistently positive but price is flat or declining, model often overestimates upside; reduce forecast by 1–3% to align with sentiment drift.
